title: Trend-aware region allocator with variant degradation safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a trend-aware region allocator that combines p50/p95 latency telemetry with lightweight network health signals to compute a blended per-region score for routing decisions. The allocator must support tiered routing (hosted/dedicated/private), per-customer overrides, and a controlled fallback mechanism that selects model variants when a preferred region degrades. Focus on: 1) robust smoothing (EWMA + windowed percentiles) to avoid flapping, 2) a single blended score that weights recency and tail latency differently, and 3) a degradation budget that triggers variant fallbacks before circuit-breaking traffic to lower tiers. Deliverable includes runtime scoring module, config knobs for weight decay and emergency thresholds, end-to-end tests, dashboards, and migration plan from current region-decider hybrid implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Blended region score computation implemented as a standalone module (p50, p95, packet-loss, retransmits) exposed via /internal/region-scores
Default score uses EWMA(5m) for p95 and 1m median for p50; decayed historical influence with configurable half-life
Routing policy uses score + tier affinity to produce a ranked region list with stable top choice >= 5 minutes under normal variance
Fallback logic selects compatible model variants by QoS budget (max 10% model-quality loss) before failing over to lower tier or alternate region
End-to-end integration tests covering: transient spike recovery, sustained p95 degradation, and network outage scenarios
Dashboard shows per-region p50/p95 trends, EWMA curves, fallback events, and per-tenant override usage
Feature rollout via runtime flag and can be toggled per-customer in console
Performance: scoring module adds <2ms median overhead to request decision path at 99th percentile under normal load
design_decisions: Use EWMA for tail (p95) to capture trend while avoiding noise; median uses short sliding window (1m) to preserve latency-sensitive assignments
Blend latency and network health by normalizing metrics into percentile ranks and summing with weights (default: 0.6 p95, 0.25 p50, 0.15 network-health)
Apply exponential decay to historical scores with configurable half-life (default 15m) to reduce flapping during rolling upgrades
Fallback selection prefers quantized model variants that preserve output quality above a degradation budget; cost-aware tie-breaker considered after quality threshold
Support per-tenant routing overrides (whitelists/blacklists) which are applied post-scoring but pre-ranking
Introduce a soft-penalty layer for regions under maintenance using annotated cluster metadata fed into the scoring pipeline
implementation_notes: Module will be implemented in runtime service region-decider v2; keep public API backward compatible via /region-decision v1 wrapper
State: store EWMA and percentile histograms in Redis with TTL equal to configured smoothing window; use atomic updates from telemetry consumer
Telemetry inputs: aggregated samples from edge collectors (p50/p95), network metrics from dataplane (packet loss, tcp_retrans) and reachability probes
Exploration: ship a low-volume randomized routing (1% traffic) to vet region-scores against ground truth for 72 hours before full rollout
Fallback budget logic: compute expected quality delta via small A/B eval harness; store variant quality scores in config service
Observability: add Prometheus metrics for score components, decision latency, and counts of fallback-trigger events; link to Grafana dashboard
